subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Reionization: Lighting Up the Cosmos
description: Learn Reionization: Lighting Up the Cosmos in one minute.

hook.text: After the Dark Ages ended, the first stars and galaxies flooded space with ultraviolet radiation.

buildup.text: This radiation stripped electrons from hydrogen atoms—re-ionizing the gas that had been neutral for millions of years.

discovery.text: Reionization turned the opaque universe transparent again. Light could travel vast distances without being absorbed.

twist.text: The process wasn't instant. It took hundreds of millions of years, with ionized bubbles slowly merging together.

climax.text: Studying reionization tells us when and how the first luminous objects turned on—the universe's cosmic dawn.

punchline.text: Stars lit up, gas cleared, and the universe became see-through again.

quiz.question: What caused reionization of the universe?
options: Ultraviolet radiation from the first stars and galaxies stripped electrons from hydrogen
A second Big Bang event released energy that ionized all matter
Dark energy heated the neutral gas until it ionized

details.summary: Reionization occurred roughly 200 million to 1 billion years after the Big Bang, as ultraviolet radiation from the first stars and galaxies stripped electrons from neutral hydrogen atoms throughout the universe.
details.whyItMatters: Reionization was the universe's last major phase transition — transforming the cosmos from a neutral fog to the transparent, ionized state it remains in today. Understanding this epoch connects the first stars to the large-scale universe we observe.
takeaways: First stars and galaxies ionized the universe's neutral hydrogen
This phase transition took from roughly 200 million to 1 billion years
It made the universe permanently transparent to UV light

faq.question: How do astronomers study reionization?
faq.answer: By observing distant quasars and galaxies whose light passed through partially neutral gas (showing absorption features) and by detecting 21-cm radio emission from neutral hydrogen. JWST's infrared capabilities allow it to see galaxies during the reionization epoch directly.

faq.question: What sources powered reionization?
faq.answer: Primarily early galaxies and their hot young stars. Active galactic nuclei (quasars) contributed as well, though their relative importance is debated. Dwarf galaxies may have produced much of the UV radiation due to their enormous numbers. The exact balance remains an active area of research.
